Signs.name: Unable to stand
Signs.farmer_text: The animal cannot rise or cannot remain standing.

Signs.name: Struggling to breathe
Signs.farmer_text: The animal is struggling to breathe, breathing with its mouth open, or its breathing is noisy.

Signs.name: Froth from the nose
Signs.farmer_text: White or clear foam or bubbles are coming from the nose.

Signs.name: Heavy bleeding
Signs.farmer_text: The animal is bleeding heavily or the bleeding will not stop.

Signs.name: Fits or unconscious
Signs.farmer_text: The animal is having fits or seizures, or is unconscious or difficult to wake.

Signs.name: Abnormal movement or behaviour
Signs.farmer_text: The animal circles, falls, presses its head against things, staggers, or cannot walk normally.

Signs.name: Severe swelling of the belly
Signs.farmer_text: The belly looks severely swollen, especially on the left side.

Signs.name: Difficulty giving birth
Signs.farmer_text: The cow is struggling to give birth.

Signs.name: Sudden death
Signs.farmer_text: An animal died suddenly.

Signs.name: Several animals sick
Signs.farmer_text: Several animals are becoming sick at the same time.

Signs.name: Reduced appetite
Signs.farmer_text: The animal is eating less, has stopped eating, or is no longer grazing.

Signs.name: Reduced cud chewing
Signs.farmer_text: The animal is chewing cud less than usual or has stopped chewing cud.

Signs.name: Drinking less
Signs.farmer_text: The animal is drinking less than usual or not drinking.

Signs.name: Weakness
Signs.farmer_text: The animal looks dull, is weak, lies down more, or struggles to move.

Signs.name: Quiet or away from the herd
Signs.farmer_text: The animal is quieter than usual, withdrawn, or staying away from the herd.

Signs.name: Lameness
Signs.farmer_text: The animal is limping, stiff, or reluctant to move.

Signs.name: Fever / feels hot
Signs.farmer_text: The animal feels unusually hot (touch the base of the ears), or a thermometer shows a high temperature.

Signs.name: Rapid breathing
Signs.farmer_text: The animal breathes quickly while resting, as if it has just been running.

Signs.name: Coughing
Signs.farmer_text: The animal is coughing.

Signs.name: Nasal discharge
Signs.farmer_text: Fluid or mucus is coming from the nose.

Signs.name: Lumps below the ear or in front of the shoulder
Signs.farmer_text: A hard lump can be seen or felt below the ear or in front of the shoulder.

Signs.name: Other swelling
Signs.farmer_text: A new lump or swelling can be seen or felt under the jaw, on the neck, legs, or belly.

Signs.name: Watery eyes
Signs.farmer_text: Tears run from the eyes more than usual.

Signs.name: Cloudy eye
Signs.farmer_text: The eye looks white, grey, milky, or covered by a film.

Signs.name: Pale inside of the eyelids
Signs.farmer_text: The inside of the eyelids looks very pale or white instead of pink.

Signs.name: Yellow eyes or gums
Signs.farmer_text: The whites of the eyes or the gums look yellow.

Signs.name: Drooling or froth from the mouth
Signs.farmer_text: Saliva or white foam is coming from the mouth.

Signs.name: Mouth sores
Signs.farmer_text: There are sores in the mouth, or the animal is drooling a lot.

Signs.name: Red or dark urine
Signs.farmer_text: The urine is red, brown, or the colour of strong tea.

Signs.name: Loose dung / diarrhoea
Signs.farmer_text: The dung is much softer or more watery than normal.

Signs.name: Blood in dung
Signs.farmer_text: There is blood in the dung.

Signs.name: Ticks
Signs.farmer_text: Ticks can be seen on the animal, especially around the ears, tail, belly, or legs.

Signs.name: Skin problem
Signs.farmer_text: There are lumps, wounds, or other changes on the skin.
